profile.reading: Per the English Wikipedia article on the National Center for Supercomputing Applications, its National Petascale Computing Facility (also called the NCSA Petascale Computing Facility) was constructed on the site of a former baseball field called Illini Field, located north of the Siebel Center for Computer Science on the University of Illinois Urbana Champaign campus. The facility has housed the Blue Waters supercomputer (NSF funded, awarded 2007) and, as of the article, houses DeltaAI, described as NCSAs latest supercomputing system. No street address, square footage, or power capacity figure is given in the article.

reading.body:
The NCSA Petascale Computing Facility in Champaign hosts research supercomputers including Blue Waters and DeltaAI, but publishes no power capacity figure, rack count, or accelerator specifications. Without disclosed capacity metrics, this facility cannot be ranked against commercial AI infrastructure or assessed for its share of grid demand. The absence of published specifications means its role in AI scaling cannot be quantified from operator data.

Illinois has 44 mapped data center facilities, of which only six publish power capacity figures totaling 236 megawatts. This campus ranks seventh in the state by published megawatts, but that ranking reflects only the six facilities that disclose capacity. Most mapped facilities in Illinois publish nothing, making state-level inference unreliable. The campus's actual capacity and position remain unknown.

NCSA Petascale Computing Facility sits on the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign campus and houses NSF-funded research systems. As an academic supercomputing center, it operates under different procurement, operational, and energy cost structures than commercial data centers. Its grid impact and scalability constraints cannot be assessed without published power specifications.
